seoDescription: Learn to build a simple and efficient REST API from scratch using Golang and the popular Gin framework. This tutorial guides you through project initialization, setting up a Gin server, and defining your first endpoints. You'll explore handling HTTP requests, returning JSON responses, and structuring your application with a clean architecture by separating logic into entities, services, and controllers. Discover how to create GET and POST endpoints to manage video data, making this a practical introduction to web development with Go.

chapters.description: Initialize a Go module, install the Gin framework dependency, and set up the initial server file.

chapters.description: Write the main function, create a default Gin server, and learn about the built-in Logger and Recovery middleware.

chapters.title: Creating a Basic GET Endpoint
chapters.description: Create a simple GET endpoint, exploring the Gin Context to handle requests and send JSON responses.

chapters.title: Running and Testing the First Endpoint
chapters.description: Start the server, understand the debug logs, and use Postman to test the newly created test endpoint.

chapters.title: Structuring the API: The Video Entity
chapters.description: Plan a three-tier architecture (entity, service, controller) and create the Video entity struct with JSON serialization tags.

chapters.title: Building the Video Service Layer
chapters.description: Define a service interface for business logic and create its implementation to save and retrieve video data using an in-memory slice.

chapters.title: Building the Video Controller Layer
chapters.description: Create the video controller interface and implementation to handle HTTP requests, bind JSON data, and delegate logic to the service layer.

chapters.title: Wiring Endpoints to the Controller
chapters.description: Integrate the service and controller into the main server file, creating GET and POST endpoints that use the controller's logic.

chapters.description: Test the complete API functionality using Postman, demonstrating how to create and then list videos.

chapters.description: A brief wrap-up of the video.

summary:
## Key Concepts for Building a REST API with Golang and Gin

This document summarizes the core steps and concepts for creating a simple REST API using the Gin framework.

### Project Setup and Server Initialization

1.  **Initialize Go Module**: Start your project with `go mod init <module_path>`.
2.  **Install Gin**: Add the Gin framework to your project using `go get github.com/gin-gonic/gin`.
3.  **Create Server Instance**: Use `server := gin.Default()` to create a router with default middleware.

> [!NOTE]
> `gin.Default()` automatically includes **Logger** and **Recovery** middleware. The Logger prints request details to the console, and Recovery prevents the server from crashing on a panic, returning a `500 Internal Server Error` instead.

4.  **Start Server**: Launch the server and make it listen for requests with `server.Run(":<port>")`, for example, `server.Run(":8080")`.

### Application Architecture

The application is structured into three main components for separation of concerns:

*   **Entity**: Go structs that model the data (e.g., `Video`). They include JSON tags for serialization/deserialization.
*   **Service**: Contains the business logic. It's defined by an interface for abstraction and implemented by a struct. In this example, it manages an in-memory slice of videos.
*   **Controller**: Handles incoming HTTP requests, validates input, calls the appropriate service methods, and returns an HTTP response.

### Handling HTTP Requests

Controllers use the `gin.Context` object to manage the HTTP request-response cycle.

*   **Defining Routes**: Routes are defined by pairing an HTTP method and a path with a handler function.
    *   `server.GET("/videos", videoController.FindAll)`
    *   `server.POST("/videos", videoController.Save)`

*   **Binding JSON**: To parse a JSON request body into a Go struct, use the `ctx.BindJSON(&yourStruct)` method. This is typically done in the controller's `Save` or `Update` methods.
    ```go
    var video entity.Video
    ctx.BindJSON(&video)
    ```

*   **Sending JSON Responses**: To send a JSON response, use `ctx.JSON(statusCode, object)`.
    ```go
    // Return a list of videos with a 200 OK status
    ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, videos)
    
    // Use gin.H for arbitrary JSON objects
    ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"message": "OK"})
    ```

> [!TIP]
> **`gin.H`** is a convenient shortcut for `map[string]interface{}`. It's useful for creating simple, unstructured JSON responses on the fly.
